sections.html:
The Wayne County Register of Deeds is at 224-226 E Walnut Street, Suite 100, Goldsboro, NC 27533. The phone is 919-731-1449 and the fax is 919-731-1441. The office page gives general hours of 8:00 to 5:00.

Real estate filings are taken from 8:00 to 4:45 without an appointment, and nothing should be walked in after 4:45 p.m. If a closing runs into the evening, send the documents by wire or electronic filing instead.

  • Real estate filings: 8:00 to 4:45
  • Vital records and notary oaths: 8:15 to 4:45
  • Marriage licenses: 8:00 to 4:00

Land records and vital records share the building, but each window keeps its own hours. Call 919-731-1449 before you drive over with anything time sensitive, so you know the right window is open.

The office is the custodian of county land and business records: deeds, deeds of trust, satisfactions and cancellations, powers of attorney, assumed business names and separation agreements. Marriage licenses, notary commissions and DD-214 discharge recordings come from the same counter.

The archive reaches back to 1913. The online index covers most real estate papers from 1971 onward, so an older tract usually means a visit in person.

Funeral homes can email registerofdeeds@waynegov.com or drop off a request, and staff call when the order is ready. Wills are not recorded here. They go to the Clerk of Courts at 919-722-6100.

The office records what is handed over. North Carolina law bars its staff from practicing law, so they will not draft a deed, explain what a form does or help fill in blanks.

Most Wayne County sales therefore run through a lawyer or title firm that prepares the deed, searches title, collects the tax and delivers the filing.

If you sell without an agent, you can still hire an attorney just for the paperwork. Ask whether the attorney will handle the recording and who pays the fees.

If you plan to skip a lawyer, call the office first and ask what the counter will and will not check. Staff can say whether a packet is in proper form to file, though they will not say whether the document does what you want.

Wayne County accepts every document type by eRecording, and its eRecording page notes that plats can now be sent this way too. Firms must pick from a list of approved vendors.

The vendor helps the firm complete a submitter agreement. Within two business days of processing it, the Register of Deeds emails an identification number, and every electronic filing needs that number.

  1. Choose an authorized vendor.
  2. Complete the submitter agreement.
  3. Receive the ID number by email.
  4. Submit deeds and deeds of trust electronically.

Vendors must hold approval under G.S. 47-14(a1). Individual sellers rarely sign up themselves, because their title company already has an account.

Recording charges under G.S. 161-10, collected at the Wayne County office
FilingCharge
Deed or other general instrument$26.00 up to 15 pages; $4.00 for every page past that
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 up to 35 pages; $4.00 each page after
Release of a loan (satisfaction)Free
Plat$21.00 a sheet
Certified copy$5.00 plus $2.00 a further page

The statute makes this schedule exclusive and requires payment before filing. Phone the office for the exact amount due on your packet.

The seller owes the state deed excise tax, paid at the Goldsboro counter before recording. The rate is one dollar for each five hundred dollars (or part) of value conveyed (G.S. 105-228.30).

You will see it on the settlement statement. Check the figure against your contract, and ask about it if the transfer is a gift or sells below market.

A deed that sits unregistered gives the buyer no protection against lien creditors or later purchasers for value (G.S. 47-18). The earlier registration wins.

You can help by clearing old liens beforehand. A paid off mortgage with no recorded satisfaction clouds the title, and lenders file releases at no charge.

  • Search the grantor index for open deeds of trust
  • Ask any lender you paid off for a satisfaction
  • Confirm the legal description matches your own vesting deed

sections.h2: How to check your title before listing
sections.html:
Run three checks before you sign a listing or an offer. They take little time and head off most closing surprises.

  • Search the online index, which covers most real estate documents from 1971, for your name as grantee and grantor.
  • Look for deeds of trust with no matching satisfaction.
  • Match your own vesting deed against the parcel shown in the county's real estate search on the tax site.

For anything before 1971, go to the Goldsboro office and ask how the older books are indexed. Staff can show you where records are kept, though they cannot interpret them.

If a plat is involved, check with the Planning Department about plats and signatures before presenting them.

sections.h2: What goes in a recording packet
sections.html:
Your closing attorney normally assembles the packet, so use this list to check their work.

  • The signed and notarized deed, with a legal description that matches the prior deed
  • A check or account for the recording charge
  • The excise tax payment, collected on the seller's side
  • A deed of trust for the buyer's lender, recorded after the deed
  • Any satisfactions for loans paid at closing

Electronic filings follow the same order, and the vendor's system carries the fee and tax figures. If something is rejected, call 919-731-1449.

sections.h2: Other Goldsboro offices in a sale
sections.html:
Three county offices come into play. The Register of Deeds records the paper. The Tax Collector, at P.O. Box 1495, supplies the tax payoff. The Clerk of Courts, at 919-722-6100, holds wills for an estate sale.

If the house belongs to an estate, call the clerk and an attorney before looking for a buyer, because the right person to sign the deed depends on what the court has done. The register of deeds will record the deed once it is signed and acknowledged, but cannot tell you whether the signer has authority.

Death certificates and other vital records come from the same Walnut Street counter, which helps an heir completing an estate file. Funeral homes are served by email, so an heir rarely needs to make a separate trip for that part.

Owners in Wayne tend to stay put, so a house may carry decades of deed history, and a buyer's title search reads all of it. An old loan that was never released is a common loose end. Median gross rent of $965 also means many sellers are landlords with rental properties to clear.

If the owner has died, the register of deeds holds the recorded chain, and the estate's attorney works from the clerk of court for the will.

faqs.q: Until what hour are real estate filings taken?
faqs.a: 4:45 p.m. The office asks people not to bring recording packages after that time, and general hours are 8:00 to 5:00.
No. Staff may not practice law, so they cannot draft a deed or explain its effect. Hire an attorney or use a closing office.

faqs.q: How far back are real estate records online?
faqs.a: Most real estate records are searchable from 1971 forward, while the archive itself goes back to 1913.

faqs.q: Is recording a loan release free?
faqs.a: Yes. State law sets no fee to record a satisfaction or cancellation of a mortgage or deed of trust.

faqs.q: Which Wayne County office takes a will?
faqs.a: The Clerk of Courts, which the Register of Deeds lists at 919-722-6100.
